2. **Resolving meaning across multiple token sets**: The same anchor appears in multiple different vocabularies/token spaces (e.g., different languages, different modalities, different model tokenizers, different contexts/sessions), and we need to determine whether the anchor refers to the same underlying concept in all of them.

4. **Meta-token coordinate layer**: A layer above raw tokens where each meta-token has coordinates (embeddings? hash-derived positions?) that allow comparison across token sets.

- Hash prefix collision rate
- Mutual information between context distributions
- Kolmogorov-style compression distance (NCD) between context bundles
